correctness.rationale: The 2025 paper proves that the canonical projection \(P\) onto \(c_{0,\mathcal I}\) for every discretely represented ideal has norm at most \(2\). The 2026 paper proves a lower bound \(2\) for the complementation constant of every proper ideal. Therefore the infimum is \(2\) and \(P\) has norm exactly \(2\). The complementary block projection \(Q\) has norm at most \(1\) because every ultrafilter-limit coefficient is bounded by the input supremum norm, and \(Q\) fixes the constant unit sequence, so its norm is exactly \(1\).

value.rationale: The theorem settles an explicit 2026 complementation-constant question on a broad natural class already central to the structure theory: all finite intersections of maximal ideals and all strongly \(\omega\)-maximal ideals. It also identifies exact norms of the canonical pair of complementary projections, which is a natural quantitative invariant rather than a routine reformulation.
